drivingQuestion: Why does Shevuot state 'two that are four' while Shabbat states eight?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa's answer stands; the יציאות wording is explained by Rav Ashi (supported by Ravina) or by Rava

segments.he: הָתָם דְּעִיקַּר שַׁבָּת הוּא, תָּנֵי אָבוֹת וְתוֹלָדוֹת. הָכָא דְּלָאו עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת הוּא – אָבוֹת תָּנֵי, וְתוֹלָדוֹת לָא תָּנֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «There,» in tractate Shabbat, «which is» where «the main» discussion of the halakhot «of Shabbat» is found, the mishna «teaches» both the «primary categories and» the «subcategories» of labor prohibited on Shabbat. But «here,» in tractate Shevuot, «which» does «not» contain «the main» discussion of the halakhot «of Shabbat,» the mishna «teaches the primary categories» of labor prohibited on Shabbat «but does not teach the subcategories» of labor.

segments.he: אָבוֹת מַאי נִינְהוּ – יְצִיאוֹת; יְצִיאוֹת תַּרְתֵּי הָוְיָין!
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What are the primary categories» of transferring an item on Shabbat? They are acts of «carrying out» from the private domain to the public domain. The Gemara objects: But the acts of «carrying out are» only «two» in number, i.e., where the carrying out is done by someone standing in the private domain and when it is done by someone in the public domain. Why then does the mishna state that there are four cases?

segments.he: וְכִי תֵּימָא: מֵהֶן לְחִיּוּב וּמֵהֶן לִפְטוּר; וְהָא דּוּמְיָא דְּמַרְאוֹת נְגָעִים קָתָנֵי – מָה הָתָם כּוּלְּהוּ לְחִיּוּבָא, אַף הָכָא כּוּלְּהוּ לְחִיּוּבָא!
segments.en: «And if you would say» that the mishna enumerates four types of carrying out, «among them» those «for» which there is «liability and among them» those «for» which there is «exemption,» that is not feasible, as «doesn’t» the mishna «teach» this case as «similar to» the different «shades of» leprous «marks?» This would indicate that «just as there, all» four «of them» are types «for» which there is «liability, so too here,» with regard to carrying out on Shabbat, «all» four «of them» are types «for» which there is «liability.»

segments.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הָתָם דְּעִיקַּר שַׁבָּת, תָּנֵי חִיּוּבֵי וּפְטוּרֵי; הָכָא, חִיּוּבֵי תָּנֵי וּפְטוּרֵי לָא תָּנֵי.
segments.en: «Rather, Rav Pappa said» that the difference between the manner in which the halakha is cited in tractates Shevuot and Shabbat must be understood as follows: «There,» in tractate Shabbat, «which» contains «the main» discussion of the halakhot «of Shabbat,» the mishna «teaches» both cases of «liability and» cases of «exemption.» But «here,» in tractate Shevuot, which does not contain the main discussion of the halakhot of Shabbat, the mishna «teaches» only cases of «liability but does not teach» cases of «exemption.»

segments.he: חִיּוּבֵי מַאי נִינְהוּ – יְצִיאוֹת; יְצִיאוֹת תַּרְתֵּי הוּא דְּהָוְיָין! שְׁתַּיִם דְּהוֹצָאָה וּשְׁתַּיִם דְּהַכְנָסָה.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What are» the cases of «liability?» They are acts of «carrying out» from the private domain to the public domain. The Gemara objects: But the acts of «carrying out are» only «two» in number. Why then does the mishna state that there are four cases? The Gemara explains: There are «two» cases «of carrying out» an item from a private domain to a public domain «and two» more cases «of bringing in» an item from a public domain to a private domain.

segments.he: וְהָא ״יְצִיאוֹת״ קָתָנֵי! אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תַּנָּא, הַכְנָסָה נָמֵי ״הוֹצָאָה״ קָרֵי לַהּ. מִמַּאי?
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «But» the mishna «teaches:» Acts of «carrying out.» It does not appear to mention acts of bringing in at all. «Rav Ashi said: The tanna also refers to» an act of «bringing in» an item «as» an act of «carrying out» an item. The Gemara asks: «From where» do we know this?

segments.he: דִּתְנַן: הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת חַיָּיב. מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן דְּקָא מְעַיֵּיל עַיּוֹלֵי – וְקָא קָרֵי לֵיהּ ״הוֹצָאָה״?
segments.en: It is «as we learned» in a mishna (Shabbat 73a): «One who carries out» an item «from» one «domain to» another «domain» is «liable.» The Gemara claims: «Are we not» also «dealing» with a case «where he is bringing» it «in» from a public domain to a private domain, «and» nevertheless the mishna «refers to it» as «carrying out?»

segments.he: וְדִלְמָא קָא מַפֵּיק מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים? אִם כֵּן, נִיתְנֵי ״הַמּוֹצִיא מֵרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד לִרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים״; מַאי ״מֵרְשׁוּת לִרְשׁוּת״? דַּאֲפִילּוּ מֵרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לִרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד,
segments.en: The Gemara questions this assertion: «But perhaps» the mishna is dealing with a case of «carrying out» an item «from a private domain to a public domain.» The Gemara defends its claim: «If so, let it» instead «teach: One who carries out» an item «from a private domain to a public domain» is liable. «What» is the reason it used the more generalized formulation: «From» one «domain to» another «domain?» To teach «that» one is liable «even» if one transfers an item «from a public domain to a private domain.»

segments.he: וְקָא קָרֵי לַהּ ״הוֹצָאָה״. וְטַעְמָא מַאי? תַּנָּא, כׇּל עֲקִירַת חֵפֶץ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ – ״הוֹצָאָה״ קָרֵי לַהּ.
segments.en: The Gemara explains further: Even though the mishna addresses carrying an item in from a public domain to a private domain, «it refers to it as carrying out.» The Gemara explains: «What is the reason» for this? «The tanna refers to any» act that involves «removal of an item from its place as carrying out.» Accordingly, the term can appropriately be used even when an item is brought in to a private domain from a public domain.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבִינָא: מַתְנִיתִין נָמֵי דַּיְקָא, דְּקָתָנֵי: ״יְצִיאוֹת שַׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בִּפְנִים וּשְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע בַּחוּץ״, וְקָא מְפָרֵשׁ הַכְנָסָה. שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ.
segments.en: «Ravina said:» The language of «the mishna» in tractate Shabbat «is also precise» in indicating this, «as it teaches:» With regard to acts of «carrying out [yetziyyot]» that are prohibited «on Shabbat,» there are primarily «two» basic actions «that are four» cases from the perspective of a person «inside» a private domain, «and two» basic actions «that are four» cases from the perspective of a person «outside,» in a public domain. «And» then, immediately, in the continuation of that mishna, «it explicates» the cases of «bringing in» an item. «Conclude from it» that the term: Carrying out, is also used to refer to bringing in an item.

segments.he: רָבָא אָמַר: רְשׁוּיוֹת קָתָנֵי – רְשׁוּיוֹת שַׁבָּת שְׁתַּיִם.
segments.en: «Rava said:» One cannot make any inference from the language of the mishna, as it is not referring to acts of carrying out. Rather, «it teaches domains.» In other words, it means: With regard to the «domains of Shabbat» there are «two» types, the existence of which leads to four types of prohibited transfers, two with regard to carrying out and two with regard to bringing in.
